title: Scalar cup on a paired resolution class
statement: For a field k, a scheme X over Spec k, a module cup resolution pairing D of F and G, and cycles a, b, c in degrees p, q, and p+q with c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val, the scalar cohomology cup of D.left.class p a and D.right.class q b equals (-1)^(p*q) times D.target.class (p+q) c.

proof.text: Choose injective comparisons for the three computing acyclic resolutions. Identify their class maps with scalar Ext representatives using the cohomology/Ext comparison. Expand the left-then-right Yoneda tensor product. Pulling the left shift out before the right shift contributes (-1)^(p*q) on the (p,q) tensor summand. The restriction-of-scalars coefficient morphism evaluates on pure sections as D.pair. The Leibniz identity makes the paired section a cocycle; hc identifies it with c. Naturality of the comparison maps then gives the stated signed equality. This complete comparison remains unformalized in the original named theorem; no equivalent scalarized hole is introduced.

theorem scalarCup_resolution_class_compatibility
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (F G : X.Modules) (p q : ℕ)
    (D : CupResolutionPairing F G)
    (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor X.toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex
      (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
    (hc : c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val) :
    scalarCohomologyCup f F G p q (D.left.class p a) (D.right.class q b) =
      (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p * q) • D.target.class (p + q) c

statement_change.what: The old unsigned normalization omits the Koszul factor. scalarExtCup composes the left class first, so extracting the left shift before the right shift on the (p,q) tensor summand contributes (-1)^(p*q). The prior module's private scalarCup_yoneda_order and oddShiftTensor_component proofs verify the order and the (1,1) sign; oddTensorSummand_ne_neg and oddShiftTensor_not_unsigned show that the sign is nontrivial over the rationals. With the resolution and front/back Cech pairings kept unsigned, the scalar cup is (-1)^(p*q) times their class. Equivalently, the Cech-to-scalar comparison has (-1)^(i.val.1*i.val.2) multiplying its left-hand side. This is a normalization correction, with no new hypotheses; p=0 or q=0, even p*q, characteristic two, and zero classes reduce to the prior formula.

old_proof.text: Choose injective-resolution comparisons for the three acyclic resolutions. The cocycle formula for moduleExtEquiv identifies each resolution class with the scalar Ext class obtained by evaluating the unit at 1. Restriction to k carries the signed Yoneda tensor construction to the sectionwise pairing D.pair, and scalarTensorCoefficient sends pure tensors to D.pair. The Leibniz equation identifies the resulting target cocycle with c. Naturality of Ext composition and homotopy independence of resolution comparisons then give the displayed equality, including degree zero, zero coefficients and empty schemes.
